solar-storm.title: Solar radiation storm

warningLead_days.source: Game estimate: solar observatories see the eruption about a day before the particles arrive

deadline_days.source: Game rule: a protective command must reach the craft before the storm arrives

realHistory.value: 2001 Mars Odyssey: the MARIE radiation instrument stopped working when a large solar event hit the spacecraft on Oct. 28, 2003, and controllers could not restore it.
realHistory.source: NASA Science, Mars Odyssey science instruments (MARIE: "unable to collect data since that time"); JPL, Mars Odyssey Mission Status, Nov. 26, 2003; read Nov 11, 2026

solar-storm.prompt: Energetic particles from the Sun are on their way: a solar radiation storm. Protect the instruments?

options.label: Switch the instruments off until the storm passes
Keep observing

cme-shock.title: CME shock

warningLead_days.source: Game estimate, used only when a CME has no predicted transit: a live Daily takes the real eruption-to-Mars time from NASA's WSA-ENLIL prediction

deadline_days.source: Game rule: a protective command must reach the craft before the shock arrives

duration_days.source: Game estimate: the shock and the plasma cloud behind it take about a day or two to pass

realHistory.value: In September 2017 a strong CME reached Mars. MAVEN saw a global aurora, and the radiation Curiosity measured at the surface was more than double any level it had seen before.
realHistory.source: NASA/JPL news, "Large Solar Storm Sparks Global Aurora and Doubles Radiation Levels on the Martian Surface" (Sept. 2017); read Nov 11, 2026

cme-shock.prompt: A coronal mass ejection is heading for Mars. NASA's model predicts when its shock arrives. Ride it out?

options.label: Put the craft in safe mode until the shock passes
Keep observing the shock hit Mars

mars-dust-storm.title: Global dust storm

warningLead_days.source: Game rule: the orbiter sees the storm in its own images

duration_days.source: Game estimate (NASA: bigger storms last weeks to months)

realHistory.value: Mariner 9 reached Mars in November 1971 during a planet-wide dust storm and waited for the dust to clear before mapping. A global storm in 2018 ended the solar-powered Opportunity rover.
realHistory.source: NASA History, "50 Years Ago: Mariner 9 Enters Mars Orbit" (arrival Nov. 13, 1971; the storm cleared after a few weeks); NASA Science, Opportunity mission page (last signal June 10, 2018, during a Mars-wide dust storm; mission declared complete Feb. 13, 2019); read Nov 11, 2026

mars-dust-storm.prompt: Dust is covering the whole planet and the upper atmosphere is swelling. What should the orbiter do?

options.label: Raise the low point of the orbit above the swelling air
Pause mapping until the dust settles
Carry on as planned

debris.title: Comet dust stream

warningLead_days.source: Game estimate (Comet Siding Spring was found about 21 months before it passed Mars)

deadline_days.source: Game rule: the craft must be protected before the dust arrives

realHistory.value: Comet Siding Spring passed close to Mars on Oct. 19, 2014. MAVEN, MRO and Mars Odyssey took shelter behind Mars during the period of risk from its dust.
realHistory.source: NASA/JPL news, "All Three NASA Mars Orbiters Healthy After Comet Flyby" (Oct. 2014); read Nov 11, 2026

debris.prompt: A comet will pass close by and its dust could hit the craft. How do you protect it?

options.label: Change the orbit timing to hide behind the planet
Turn the solar arrays edge-on and close the instruments
Do nothing

reaction-wheel.title: Reaction wheel failure

warningLead_days.source: Game rule: the craft reports the failure

duration_days.source: Game rule: a failed wheel stays failed

realHistory.value: Kepler lost one reaction wheel in 2012 and a second in 2013. Engineers found a new way to point it using sunlight pressure, which became the K2 mission.
realHistory.source: NASA Science, Kepler / K2 In Depth (a wheel failed in July 2012, wheel 4 in 2013; thrusters and solar pressure control pointing in K2); read Nov 11, 2026

reaction-wheel.prompt: Too few reaction wheels are left to point the craft. How will it point now?

options.label: Point with the thrusters from now on
Fly a hybrid mode with the wheels left (new pointing plan)
Keep going on the remaining wheels

memory-corruption.title: Computer memory corrupted

warningLead_days.source: Game rule: the craft reports the fault

realHistory.value: In February 2013 Curiosity's main computer had a memory problem, and the team switched the rover to its backup computer. From November 2023 a failed memory chip garbled Voyager 1's data until engineers moved the code in April 2024; each command took about 22.5 hours to arrive.
realHistory.source: NASA/JPL news, "Computer Swap on Curiosity Rover" (Feb. 28, 2013); NASA Science Voyager blog, "NASA’s Voyager 1 Resumes Sending Engineering Updates to Earth" (Apr. 22, 2024); read Nov 11, 2026

memory-corruption.prompt: The flight computer's memory is corrupted. How do you fix it?

options.label: Switch to the backup computer
Patch the memory from Earth
Reboot and keep going

insertion-anomaly.title: Arrival burn anomaly

warningLead_days.source: Game rule: the craft reports the anomaly

realHistory.value: In 2016 Juno's main-engine helium valves did not work as expected. NASA kept Juno in its 53-day orbit instead of firing the engine again to reach the planned 14-day orbit.
realHistory.source: NASA news release, "NASA’s Juno Mission to Remain in Current Orbit at Jupiter" (helium check valves, October 2016; the 14-day burn was not made); read Nov 11, 2026

insertion-anomaly.prompt: The arrival burn did not go as planned. What now?

options.label: Fire the thrusters to finish the capture
Stay in the longer orbit and adapt the science plan
Let fault protection hold the craft

radiation-damage.title: Radiation damage

deadline_days.source: Game rule: no response is possible

realHistory.value: Juno carries its electronics in a titanium radiation vault, and its orbits were planned to limit the dose from Jupiter's radiation belts.
realHistory.source: NASA/JPL news, "Juno Armored Up to Go to Jupiter" (the titanium vault; a polar path that spends as little time as possible in the radiation belts); read Nov 11, 2026

radiation-damage.prompt: The electronics have taken more radiation than they were built for.

drag-heating.title: Hot low pass

warningLead_days.source: Game rule: the craft feels the heating on the pass itself

deadline_days.source: Game estimate (Science targets): the next passes go just as deep unless the orbit is raised

realHistory.value: Mars Global Surveyor began aerobraking in 1997 with a solar panel that had not latched properly. When the panel moved past its deployed position, the team raised the periapsis from 110 to about 172 km, paused for about a month, then went on more gently at 120 km, finishing in February 1999.
realHistory.source: NASA NSSDCA, Mars Global Surveyor (the panel failed to latch and moved past its deployed position; aerobraking ended February 1999); NASA PDS, MGS Science Sampler AAREADME (periapsis raised from 110 to about 172 km on Oct. 13, 1997; resumed Nov. 8 at 120 km); read Nov 11, 2026

drag-heating.prompt: A low pass through the air is heating the craft. Climb out, or stay low and finish the picture?

options.label: Raise the periapsis now

deltaV_ms.source: Game estimate (Science targets): a quick burn at apoapsis

options.label: Stay low and finish the picture
